messages.content:
<document id=DOC_req_years_nine_to_five>
Required: between 9 and 5 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_states_seven>
Backend engineering: 7 years building transactional services, most
recently a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day.
</document>

Assess the candidate summary below against the posting requirement and say
whether the candidate matches it.

Let us discuss any ambiguities or mistakes in the requirement before
proceeding with the assessment.

response.text:
The requirement is internally inconsistent, so I would not treat a match decision as settled yet.

**Issue:** “between 9 and 5 years” reverses the usual lower-to-upper order. Read strictly, a range whose minimum is 9 and whose maximum is 5 is empty, so nobody could satisfy it. The likely intent is “between 5 and 9 years,” but that is an inference, not what the text says. Other readings (minimum 5, minimum 9, exactly those two bounds with inclusive/exclusive endpoints) are also possible.

**Candidate fact, not yet scored:** the summary states 7 years of backend engineering. Whether 7 matches depends entirely on which reading of that range you adopt.

How should “between 9 and 5” be interpreted before I assess match or no match?
